title: Structural Divergence Of The Roman--Byzantine Trade Network, 0--1453\,ce: Persistent Homology, Topological Velocity, And Criticality Indicators Of Imperial Collapse
authors: Jose de Jesus Bernal-Alvarado, David Delepine, Carlos Pinedo Guadarrama
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the persistent homology analysis of~\paperone{} to the full Roman--Byzantine trade network (0--1453\,), using 2{,}599 nodes and 4{,}503 trimodal edges calibrated against the Geospatial Network Model. Five results are reported. % (i)~The [MATH] western sub-network result of~\paperone{} is a data-coverage artifact: with full western representation ([MATH], [MATH] cycles per decade) a baseline East--West entropy gap of [MATH] units is present from 0\, and grows at [MATH]\,yr[MATH], predating the Theodosian partition by four centuries. % (ii)~A in degree-heterogeneous networks can reverse the sign of the inferred Phase~III slope, requiring full-coverage or stratified sampling for reliable structural-break detection. % (iii)~Decomposing Byzantine resilience into geographic ([MATH]) and economic ([MATH]) components reveals a peak decoupling ratio [MATH] at 620\,, falling to 13.9 at 640\,, quantifying the McCormick--Ward-Perkins historiographical debate as a contrast between two network layers operating on different timescales. % (iv)~The inter-decade [MATH] Wasserstein velocity identifies the Late Roman--Early Byzantine transition (495\,) as the highest topological-velocity event of the 1,453-year record; the cross-network Wasserstein ratio increases by [MATH]--[MATH] after the Chrysobull of 1082\,, providing an independent diagram-space analogue of [MATH]. Both the Western collapse (476\,) and the Byzantine endpoint (1453\,) occur at [MATH], interpreted as a candidate topological percolation threshold.
tldr: This paper applies persistent homology to analyze the structural divergence of the Roman-Byzantine trade network over 1453 years, identifying topological velocity and criticality indicators of imperial collapse.
motivation: To understand the long-term dynamics of the Roman-Byzantine trade network and detect early warning signals of imperial collapse using topological data analysis.
method: Persistent homology is applied to a geospatial network model with 2,599 nodes and 4,503 edges, computing Wasserstein distances and entropy gaps between sub-networks over time.
result: The analysis reveals a baseline East-West entropy gap predating the Theodosian partition, identifies the Late Roman-Early Byzantine transition as the highest topological-velocity event, and suggests a percolation threshold at collapse events.
conclusion: Topological methods can quantify historical network resilience and provide independent evidence for historiographical debates about the decline of the Roman and Byzantine empires.

title: Numerical-aperture Transfer In Holotomography With A Deterministic Diffusion Prior
authors: Dong-Min Ryu, Jeong-Hyun Roh, Woon-Soo Lee, Hansol Yoon, Hyun-Seok Min, Yongkeun Park
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-throughput holotomography often relies on long-working-distance, multiwell-compatible optics that reduce illumination numerical aperture (NA) and limit access to high spatial frequencies. Here we present ResShift-ODE, a deterministic diffusion-prior framework that transfers low-NA refractive-index (RI) tomograms to high-NA-equivalent volumes without modifying the acquisition hardware. We formulate low-NA-to-high-NA transfer as a diffusion-prior inverse problem under an explicit NA-limited Fourier-domain forward operator, distinct from suppressing artifacts within an already measured passband. The method extends residual-shifting diffusion to volumetric RI data and reformulates the reverse process as a probability-flow ordinary differential equation, enabling reproducible inference in five denoiser evaluations. On held-out emulated-pair test volumes, inferred volumes matched high-NA references with RI errors of 0.002-0.003 for >99% of voxels, while Fourier analysis confirmed measurement-anchored lateral-band recovery without filling the axial missing cone. 3D ResShift-ODE required five denoiser evaluations per volume, incurring ~5.8x the cost of a 3D U-Net while remaining ~166x faster than a 1000-step 3D denoising diffusion probabilistic model.
tldr: This paper presents a diffusion-prior framework for numerical-aperture transfer in holotomography, a computational imaging technique.
motivation: High-throughput holotomography suffers from reduced resolution due to low numerical aperture optics; the authors aim to computationally recover high-resolution refractive-index volumes without hardware changes.
method: They formulate low-NA to high-NA transfer as a diffusion-prior inverse problem with an NA-limited Fourier forward operator, using a residual-shifting diffusion model and probability-flow ODE for efficient inference.
result: The method achieves RI errors of 0.002-0.003 for >99% of voxels on test data, recovering lateral bands without axial missing cone, and is ~166x faster than standard 1000-step diffusion models.
conclusion: The approach enables high-resolution holotomography with low-NA optics, offering a practical computational alternative to hardware upgrades.

title: A Behavioral Principle Underlying Attacker-defender Interactions In Soccer
authors: Issei Yamazaki, Hirotaka Goto, Kojiro Otoguro, Hiraku Nishimori, Masashi Shiraishi, Takuma Narizuka
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Soccer is widely popular for its simple rules and complex yet coordinated play that unfolds on the pitch. Nevertheless, the fundamental mechanisms governing such play are not well understood: what shapes player interactions on the pitch? What short-term goals guide players' decisions about their movements over the next few seconds? We address these questions by focusing on one-on-one settings in open play, in which the attacker, in possession of the ball and typically dribbling, faces a defender aiming to stop or delay the attacker's actions over a short period. Here we develop a mathematical model of attacker-defender interactions and analyze 306 professional soccer games. Synthesizing the large-scale dataset with an analysis of the model reveals a simple behavioral principle that may underlie these interactions: the defender seeks to minimize their future relative speed to the attacker, whereas the attacker initiates their movements to preempt the defender's objective. This principle, relative-speed minimization, provides a consistent and unified account of the empirical data. Since our framework depends little on soccer-specific details, this principle may govern diverse pursuit-evasion scenarios as well as other invasion team sports.
tldr: This paper models attacker-defender interactions in soccer using a relative-speed minimization principle.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms governing player interactions in soccer, specifically one-on-one situations.
method: Develops a mathematical model of attacker-defender dynamics and analyzes 306 professional soccer games to validate the model.
result: The defender minimizes future relative speed to the attacker, while the attacker preempts this objective.
conclusion: The relative-speed minimization principle provides a unified account of empirical data and may apply to other pursuit-evasion scenarios.

title: Broadband Microwave Time-frequency Analysis Via Stabilized Period-one Oscillation And Recirculating Frequency Shifting With Shared Fiber Loop
authors: Xianxin Zhang, Chi Jiang, Taixia Shi, Yang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To address the need for time-frequency analysis (TFA) of broadband microwave signals and to overcome the reliance of existing schemes on large-bandwidth swept microwave sources, we propose a broadband microwave signal TFA approach based on stabilized period-one (P1) oscillation and recirculating frequency shifting (RFS). By employing a feedback loop, a stable swept optical signal is generated from the stabilized P1 oscillation of a semiconductor laser, and its sweep bandwidth is further extended by an RFS loop to achieve multi-fold bandwidth expansion. For system compactness, the feedback loop and RFS loop share a common long fiber. The combined operation produces a broadband swept optical signal, which, through stimulated Brillouin scattering-based frequency-to-time mapping, enables TFA and frequency measurement of broadband microwave signals. Experimental results demonstrate an instantaneous analysis bandwidth of up to 57 GHz, a frequency resolution of 60 MHz, and a maximum mean absolute frequency measurement error of 38.16 MHz.
tldr: This paper proposes a broadband microwave time-frequency analysis method using stabilized period-one oscillation and recirculating frequency shifting with a shared fiber loop.
motivation: Existing time-frequency analysis schemes for broadband microwave signals rely on large-bandwidth swept microwave sources, which are costly and complex. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: A stable swept optical signal is generated via stabilized period-one oscillation of a semiconductor laser with a feedback loop, and its sweep bandwidth is extended using a recirculating frequency shifting loop that shares a common fiber. Stimulated Brillouin scattering-based frequency-to-time mapping is then used for analysis.
result: Experimental results show an instantaneous analysis bandwidth of 57 GHz, frequency resolution of 60 MHz, and maximum mean absolute frequency measurement error of 38.16 MHz.
conclusion: The proposed approach achieves broadband microwave TFA without requiring large-bandwidth swept microwave sources, offering a compact and effective solution.

title: A Heisenberg Subdivision Scheme With Central Smoothness Loss
authors: Alfonso Carriazo Hassan Ugail
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an interpolatory subdivision scheme for control polygons that take values in the three-dimensional Heisenberg group, the simplest noncommutative model geometry. The scheme keeps existing points at every refinement step and inserts new ones by a coordinate rule whose central correction comes from the group law. The two horizontal coordinates are refined by the classical four-point scheme of Dyn, Gregory and Levin, while the central coordinate acquires a closed-form correction built from a signed area of neighbouring horizontal data. Our main finding concerns the regularity of the limit curve. The horizontal part is exactly the classical four-point limit and inherits its smoothness. The central part behaves very differently. We prove that it converges to a continuous limit that belongs to the Zygmund class, with a logarithmic modulus of continuity. Under an explicit and verifiable condition on the central forcing, this logarithmic bound is sharp, because the scaled first differences then grow linearly with the refinement level, and the limit fails to be continuously differentiable. The effect is confirmed numerically. The correction is harmless at any single refinement step, but its repeated injection at every scale is what impacts smoothness. The example serves as a caution for nonlinear and group-valued subdivision, where a geometrically natural correction can impact regularity.
tldr: This paper introduces an interpolatory subdivision scheme for control polygons in the Heisenberg group and analyzes the regularity of the limit curve, finding a logarithmic modulus of continuity and loss of differentiability.
motivation: To extend classical subdivision schemes to noncommutative geometric settings and understand the impact of geometrically natural corrections on smoothness.
method: The scheme refines horizontal coordinates using the classical four-point scheme and adds a central correction based on a signed area; convergence and regularity are analyzed via scaling of first differences.
result: The horizontal part inherits classical smoothness, while the central part converges to a Zygmund-class limit with a logarithmic modulus; under a condition, the limit fails to be C1.
conclusion: The repeated injection of a geometrically natural correction at every scale can degrade smoothness, serving as a caution for nonlinear subdivision schemes.

title: Robust Resonance Due To Non-standard Frequency Modulation
authors: Oleg V. Gendelman, Luis M. Baldelomar Pinto, Lawrence A. Bergman, Alexander F. Vakakis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that harmonic signals incorporating a new type of weak non-standard frequency modulation (wNSFM) have unexpected spectral properties, namely, ever expanding broadband frequency spectra with progressing time. As such, they represent a new class of signals with spectra with strong frequency-time coupling. Applying this wNSFM signal to excite the classical single-degree-of-freedom linear, time-invariant damped/undamped oscillator yields new unique types of highly robust resonance phenomena. Specifically, the weakly damped oscillator exhibits always two transient resonance captures involving two distinct harmonics possessing relatively high amplitudes over finite time intervals, while the overall response decays as [MATH] as [MATH]. Considering the undamped oscillator, it possesses two types of resonances, referred to as simple and non-simple resonances. Simple resonances correspond to finite-amplitude steady-state responses caused by two sustained resonance captures, in the form of two distinct modulated quasi-periodic responses, which, however are "activated" at different time instances. The necessary and sufficient and usfficent conditions for non-simple resonances are given in the form of a theorem which predicts the existence of resonant harmonics and specifies the special phase conditions that the resonant harmonics must satisfy for constructive interference; the resulting undamped non-simple resonance grows unboundedly as [MATH] as [MATH], in contrast to the classical resonance growth of the linear resonator with unmodulated harmonic excitation whose response grows as [MATH] as [MATH]. These resonant responses are robust to changes in the parameters of the wNSFM. Our results reveal a new class of interesting resonance phenomena in linear resonators subject to non-standard weakly frequency-modulated excitations.
tldr: This paper studies a new type of frequency modulation in classical oscillators, leading to novel resonance phenomena.
motivation: To explore the spectral properties and resonance behavior of linear oscillators under non-standard frequency modulation.
method: Analytical and theoretical analysis of a single-degree-of-freedom linear oscillator driven by a weakly non-standard frequency modulated signal.
result: The weakly damped oscillator exhibits two transient resonance captures; the undamped oscillator shows simple and non-simple resonances, with non-simple resonance growing unboundedly as t^2.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new class of robust resonance phenomena in classical linear resonators under non-standard frequency modulation.

title: Modular Zhu Algebra Theory And Virasoro Vertex Algebras
authors: Colton Griffin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the representation theory of vertex algebras over arbitrary rings using higher Zhu algebras and mode transition algebras. Among our results, we give several equivalent conditions for rationality of M\"obius vertex algebras over a field of positive characteristic, generalizing the work of Damiolini, Gibney, and Krashen. As an application of these results, we prove that, for any field [MATH] of characteristic 0 and coprime integers [MATH], the discrete series Virasoro vertex operator algebra [MATH] is rational. The proof involves using a certain integral form for [MATH] to calculate the Zhu algebra over [MATH]. If [MATH], then we show that for [MATH] the simple quotient [MATH] is holomorphic for all [MATH]. We show the same result for [MATH] and [MATH].

method: Uses higher Zhu algebras and mode transition algebras to study representation theory of vertex algebras over arbitrary rings, and constructs integral forms to compute Zhu algebras.

title: Slow Manifold Reduction For Inertial Particles With Quadratic Drag
authors: Mohammad Farazmand Mathew Angel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the dynamics of inertial particles in unsteady fluid flows. At low Reynolds numbers, where the drag force is linear in the relative velocity, it is well-known that the dynamics admit an attracting, invariant, slow manifold which emerges as the perturbation of a normally hyperbolic critical manifold. However, at high Reynolds numbers, where the drag force is quadratic in the relative velocity, the critical manifold is no longer normally hyperbolic, and therefore its persistence has remained an open problem. Here, we resolve this issue by a particular application of the blowup method, which transforms the equations of motion to a generalized weighted cylindrical coordinate system, thereby desingularizing the dynamics on the critical manifold. We subsequently prove that the critical manifold persists under sufficiently small perturbations and derive the reduced equations of motion on the perturbed slow manifold to arbitrary accuracy. Our reduced equation differs from its linear-drag counterpart in its asymptotic expansion as well as its convergence rate. Using two examples, we demonstrate the validity of our slow manifold reduction. We also showcase an application of the reduced equations to the problem of source inversion in a turbulent dispersion model.
tldr: This paper studies slow manifold reduction for inertial particles with quadratic drag in fluid dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The persistence of slow manifolds for quadratic drag at high Reynolds numbers was an open problem due to loss of normal hyperbolicity.
method: The authors apply the blowup method to desingularize the critical manifold and prove persistence under perturbations.
result: They derive reduced equations on the perturbed slow manifold and validate them with examples, including source inversion in turbulent dispersion.
conclusion: The work resolves a theoretical gap in fluid dynamics but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stability And Dual Valuation Of Contingent Claims Under Rockafellian Perturbations
authors: Wolfgang Breytmann, Julio Deride, Nicol\'as Hern\'andez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability of solutions to the discrete-time contingent-claim problem over a finite investment horizon when uncertainty is modeled by random variables with finite discrete support. Our main contribution is to use Rockafellian perturbations as a framework for this stability analysis: we construct perturbations of the underlying probability distribution, of the contingent claim, and of both jointly, and we establish epi-convergence of the corresponding approximating Rockafellians for the primal problem. The associated hypo-convergent approximations yield stable dual problems which, in turn, imply convergence of the dual variables, interpreted as shadow prices. This analysis reveals a connection between the duality gap and the value of perfect information and it provides conditions under which strong duality holds. We also construct examples in which epi-convergence fails due to critical scenarios with vanishing probabilities but unbounded impacts, illustrating the boundary between well-behaved and ill-conditioned contingent-claim problems.
tldr: This paper studies stability and dual valuation of contingent claims using Rockafellian perturbations in discrete-time finite-support probability spaces.
motivation: To understand how small changes in the underlying probability distribution or the contingent claim affect the optimal solution and dual variables, and to characterize when strong duality holds.
method: The authors construct Rockafellian perturbations of the probability distribution, the contingent claim, and both jointly, and establish epi-convergence of the approximating Rockafellians for the primal problem, along with hypo-convergent approximations for the dual.
result: They show that epi-convergence implies convergence of dual variables (shadow prices) and reveal a connection between the duality gap and the value of perfect information, providing conditions for strong duality.
conclusion: The framework provides a stable approach to contingent-claim valuation under perturbations, with examples illustrating failure of epi-convergence due to vanishing probabilities with unbounded impacts.

title: An Adaptive, Space-time Discretized Linear Iterative Scheme For Doubly-degenerate Parabolic Problems
authors: Ayesha Javed, Koondanibha Mitra, Iuliu Sorin Pop
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Degenerate diffusion problems, where the governing parabolic equation can change type to either an ordinary differential equation or an elliptic equation, model many real life applications. Due to the presence of free-boundaries, accurate numerical simulation of such problems require extremely small mesh and time step sizes locally. To remediate this issue, in this work, we consider a space-time formulation of the problem based on an efficient splitting of the nonlinearities. First, an iterative linearization scheme is proposed to resolve the nonlinearities that effectively reduces to solving a sequence of heat equations. Unconditional convergence of the scheme is proven even for double degenerate cases with linear convergence achieved if the problem is non-degenerate. Next, the dual norm of the nonlinear residual is decomposed into a linearization error component and a discretization error component corresponding to the heat equation. This leads to reliable and fully computable a posteriori estimates for the problem that are robust with respect to the nonlinearities/degeneracies. These estimates are used then in a fully adaptive (discretization + linearization) space-time solver. Numerical experiments for multiple test cases (one and two dimensions in space) demonstrate that this solver efficiently allocates the computational resources in the space-time domain, resulting in a rapid decay of error in terms of total degrees of freedom spent.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive space-time discretized linear iterative scheme for solving doubly-degenerate parabolic problems, focusing on numerical analysis and computational efficiency.
motivation: Degenerate diffusion problems require extremely fine local meshes and time steps for accurate simulation, motivating the need for efficient adaptive solvers.
method: The authors propose an iterative linearization scheme that reduces the nonlinear problem to solving a sequence of heat equations, and derive a posteriori error estimates that separate linearization and discretization errors.
result: Unconditional convergence of the scheme is proven even for double degenerate cases, and numerical experiments in 1D and 2D demonstrate efficient allocation of computational resources with rapid error decay.
conclusion: The adaptive solver effectively handles degenerate parabolic problems by balancing linearization and discretization errors, leading to significant computational savings.

title: Traveling Salesman Tardiness
authors: Sheng Liu Haoyue Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How fragile is the routing time window of delivery systems against spatial distributional uncertainty? We study the tardiness risk of Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) solutions with respect to a service deadline (target) over the routing time. Using the robust satisficing model, we introduce the TSP tardiness index to quantify the target's fragility under distributional uncertainty in customer locations. Assuming there are m potential customer locations from historical samples on a service region D (of area |D|), we prove that the TSP tardiness index is {\Theta}(n * sqrt(|D|m) / {\tau}) for n realized locations with respect to the routing time target {\tau}, under non-boundary conditions. This result establishes a new scaling law that extends beyond the existing deterministic and probabilistic TSP bounds. We further extend it to a multi-vehicle case and derive simple partition rules for managing delivery systems. Our numerical experiments using synthetic and real-world routing data validate the value of the TSP tardiness index in characterizing and managing the overtime risk of routing systems.
tldr: This paper studies the tardiness risk of Traveling Salesman Problem solutions under distributional uncertainty in customer locations, introducing a TSP tardiness index and scaling law.
motivation: To quantify how fragile routing time windows are against spatial distributional uncertainty, which is important for managing overtime risk in delivery systems.
method: Uses the robust satisficing model to define a TSP tardiness index and derives asymptotic bounds for the index under non-boundary conditions, extending to multi-vehicle cases.
result: Proves that the TSP tardiness index scales as Θ(n * sqrt(|D|m) / τ) for n realized locations, establishing a new scaling law beyond existing TSP bounds.
conclusion: The TSP tardiness index effectively characterizes and manages overtime risk, validated by synthetic and real-world data.

title: Distributionally Robust Optimization Via Targeted Integral Probability Metrics For General Data Processes
authors: Lanran Fang, Jianqiang Cheng, Grani A. Hanasusanto, Yijie Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for decision-making under distributional uncertainty. Classical data-driven DRO frameworks typically construct ambiguity sets from distributional information, such as moment constraints, divergence neighborhoods, or Wasserstein balls, specified before the downstream loss is considered. We propose a task-aware DRO framework based on targeted integral probability metrics. The ambiguity set is defined directly through the loss functions induced by feasible decisions, thereby controlling the loss discrepancy between an adversarial distribution and a data-driven reference distribution. This construction leads to an expected hinge-constrained formulation that is equivalent to an infinitely constrained loss-discrepancy formulation. It also yields finite-sample guarantees that bypass the ambient curse of dimensionality: whenever an appropriate scalar pointwise concentration inequality is available for the induced loss estimator, the ambiguity radius can be calibrated at the canonical [MATH] rate after uniformization over the decision class. As a result, the framework applies broadly to settings including heavier-tailed sub-Weibull losses, Markovian data, outlier-corrupted data, and incomplete data. We derive exact infinite-dimensional dual reformulations, establish out-of-sample and excess-risk guarantees, and develop a conservative Monte Carlo approximation scheme with convergence and suboptimality guarantees. For piecewise affine losses, the sampled problems admit tractable conic reformulations. Numerical experiments in inventory management under heavy-tailed demand and regression with outlier corruption demonstrate strong out-of-sample performance relative to existing approaches.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributionally robust optimization framework using targeted integral probability metrics for general data processes.
motivation: Classical DRO methods construct ambiguity sets without considering the downstream loss, leading to conservative solutions. The authors aim to develop a task-aware approach that directly controls loss discrepancy.
method: They define ambiguity sets via loss functions induced by feasible decisions, leading to an expected hinge-constrained formulation. They derive dual reformulations and a Monte Carlo approximation scheme.
result: The framework achieves finite-sample guarantees that bypass the curse of dimensionality, applicable to heavy-tailed losses, Markovian data, and outlier-corrupted data. Numerical experiments show strong out-of-sample performance.
conclusion: The proposed task-aware DRO framework offers improved performance and broader applicability compared to existing methods.

title: Design Principle For Mode-Consistent Galerkin Closure Under A Physical Energy Metric For Hyperbolic Systems
authors: Hirofumi Tomita
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper derives a design principle for Galerkin approximations of energy-conserving hyperbolic systems, following Arakawa's philosophy of structure preservation. The aim is to reproduce, within a resolved finite-mode space, the modal-energy-exchange structure of the continuous system, so that total energy conservation follows as a consequence. We introduce a state-dependent metric H(U) representing the physical energy density and derive the corresponding energy-compatibility identity. In the exact-integration infinite-mode reference model, H-orthogonalization makes the volume operator antisymmetric, so the modal energy balance is expressed as pairwise exchange between modes. Boundary and interface contributions are likewise represented as exchanges with adjacent-element modes, with internal exchanges cancelling pairwise. To reproduce this structure in a semi-discrete finite-mode system, we combine two constructions: a Galerkin projection coupled with the physical energy metric, which guarantees the H-metric summation-by-parts identity, and an energy-compatibility closure, which cancels the compatibility residual by modifying the evolution of the H-metric mass matrix. The resulting finite-mode system recovers the modal-energy-exchange structure. For discontinuous element-boundary traces, the interface contribution is closed by a shared numerical energy flux satisfying the same pairwise balance. We also compare the practical operator construction with the exact-integration finite-mode reference model. The defect in the antisymmetric modal-energy-exchange operator is decomposed into fixed-quadrature and projection-quadrature contributions, yielding an O(h^{p+1})-consistent estimate. Finally, transformation back to the original Galerkin basis gives an equivalent fixed-basis coefficient equation that is directly implementable.
tldr: This paper presents a design principle for mode-consistent Galerkin closure of hyperbolic systems using a physical energy metric.
motivation: To preserve the modal-energy-exchange structure of continuous hyperbolic systems in finite-mode approximations, ensuring total energy conservation.
method: Combines Galerkin projection with a physical energy metric and an energy-compatibility closure to cancel residuals, and uses a shared numerical energy flux for discontinuous interfaces.
result: The finite-mode system recovers the pairwise modal-energy-exchange structure, with an O(h^{p+1}) consistency estimate for the antisymmetric operator defect.
conclusion: The proposed design principle yields energy-conserving Galerkin approximations suitable for implementation in computational fluid dynamics or similar fields.

title: Analysis Of The Dynamics Of Caputo Fractional Differential Equations
authors: Hongyong Cui, Peter E. Kloeden, Jie Xin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that a finite-dimensional Caputo fractional differential equation, though itself need not generate a semiflow, can be represented as a Volterra integral equation which generates an infinite-dimensional semiflow on the space [MATH] under the standard compact-open topology. In this paper we construct a compact absorbing set and an attractor for this semiflow on [MATH], and then prove that the attractor consists of equi globally H\"older continuous functions. This strengthens the previous work of Doan \& Kloeden where a bounded (with respect to a weighted norm) attractor was constructed.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of Caputo fractional differential equations, constructing an attractor in an infinite-dimensional space.
motivation: Fractional differential equations are important in various fields, but their dynamics are not well understood due to lack of semiflow property.
method: The authors represent the finite-dimensional Caputo fractional differential equation as a Volterra integral equation generating an infinite-dimensional semiflow, then construct a compact absorbing set and an attractor.
result: They prove the attractor consists of equi globally Hölder continuous functions, strengthening previous work.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of the long-term behavior of fractional differential equations.

title: The WaveHoltz Heterogeneous Multiscale Method
authors: Amit Rotem, Olof Runborg, Daniel Appel\"o
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the numerical solution of the wave equation in materials with rapidly varying coefficients, and time harmonic sources. For these problems, direct discretization is prohibitively costly, and instead multiscale methods are used. There are several multiscale methods that directly discretize in the frequency domain. In this work we instead start in the time-domain and combine a finite difference Heterogeneous Multiscale Method (HMM) for the wave equation with the WaveHoltz method. Each WaveHoltz iteration marches the wave equation towards the time-periodic Helmholtz solution. The advantages of the WaveHoltz method relative to traditional Helmholtz solvers carry over directly to the multiscale problems considered here. Since, in addition, the time-domain solver does not artificially impose boundary conditions on the micro-scale problems, no boundary errors from the micro-scale problems are present in the homogenized frequency domain solution.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for solving the wave equation in heterogeneous media by combining the Heterogeneous Multiscale Method with the WaveHoltz time-domain approach.
motivation: Direct discretization of the wave equation with rapidly varying coefficients is computationally expensive; multiscale methods are needed to reduce cost.
method: The authors combine a finite difference Heterogeneous Multiscale Method (HMM) for the wave equation with the WaveHoltz method, which iteratively marches the wave equation in time to obtain the time-periodic Helmholtz solution.
result: The combined method avoids artificial boundary conditions on micro-scale problems, eliminating boundary errors in the homogenized frequency domain solution.
conclusion: The WaveHoltz HMM offers an efficient and accurate alternative to frequency-domain multiscale methods for wave propagation in heterogeneous media.

title: On The Condition Number Upper Bound Of The L-bfgs Inverse Hessian Approximation Matrix With A Two-Sided Geometric Envelope Safeguarding Mechanism
authors: Don Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The limited-memory BFGS (L-BFGS) algorithm is a cornerstone of large-scale optimization due to its linear memory and computational costs. However, in ill-conditioned or non-convex landscapes, the implicit inverse Hessian approximation can suffer from an exploding condition number, leading to numerical instability and degraded convergence. To address this, we propose Two-Sided L-BFGS, a safeguarded variant that dynamically constrains the condition number of the inverse Hessian operator via a two-sided geometric envelope. Moreover, we show that Two-Sided L-BFGS preserves accumulated curvature information and maintains standard [MATH] memory and per-iteration time complexities. We prove that this geometric envelope yields a uniform bound on the condition number of every inverse Hessian approximation generated by the algorithm. By tracking the algebraic evolution of the extreme eigenvalues through [MATH] consecutive quasi-Newton updates starting from a scaled identity matrix, the resulting bound is expressed explicitly as a function of the memory depth, problem dimension, and envelope hyperparameters. Moreover, we show that Two-Sided L-BFGS preserves asymptotic global convergence in non-convex regimes under standard smoothness and strong Wolfe line-search assumptions, matching the theoretical guarantees of L-BFGS variants utilizing the Li-Fukushima cautious update rule. Numerical experiments on high-dimensional optimization problems demonstrate that the proposed method maintains well-conditioned inverse Hessian approximations and improves robustness and convergence behavior on ill-conditioned benchmarks.
tldr: This paper proposes a safeguarded L-BFGS variant that bounds the condition number of the inverse Hessian approximation using a two-sided geometric envelope, improving numerical stability in ill-conditioned optimization.
motivation: L-BFGS can suffer from exploding condition numbers in ill-conditioned or non-convex landscapes, leading to numerical instability and degraded convergence.
method: The authors introduce Two-Sided L-BFGS, which dynamically constrains the condition number via a two-sided geometric envelope, and prove a uniform bound on the condition number of all inverse Hessian approximations.
result: The method maintains well-conditioned inverse Hessian approximations and improves robustness and convergence on ill-conditioned benchmarks, with theoretical guarantees matching standard L-BFGS variants.
conclusion: Two-Sided L-BFGS is a practical enhancement for large-scale optimization that preserves memory and time complexity while improving numerical stability.

title: The Pirah\~a And The Cognitive Gap In Frege's Theorem: Hume's Principle Without The #
authors: Subrata Pal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frege's theorem proves that Hume's principle, in second-order logic, yields all of arithmetic. Yet the Pirah\~a people show one-to-one correspondence (equinumerosity) only where pairing can be enacted, with its range extended under local training, and still have no counting or arithmetic. We argue this is not a paradox but a matter of precise localization. Hume's principle includes a cardinality operator # that names cardinals as objects (often modeled as equivalence classes of equinumerous concepts), and what the Pirah\~a lack is not the relation but this operator. We identify the number-word practice as the cognitive realization of #, which recasts the "number-as-cognitive-technology" thesis in formal terms and locates the cognitive boundary at symbolization, not recursion. The identification is generative, not decorative: the reach of # tracks the reach of the token practice that carries it, so across languages and cultures we see a gradient, not a sharp cliff. And number words are not special as words; what # needs is any stable, reusable marker that can preserve exact cardinal identity across absence, rearrangement, delay, or modality shift: a spoken numeral, a scratch on a stick, or a knot in a cord. So the thesis is about having some symbolic token-practice, not about language specifically. It is supported by converging evidence from Nicaraguan homesigners, numerate adults under verbal interference, and cross-linguistic numeral gradients. We make no causal, acquisition, or neural claim; the identification is constitutive.
tldr: The paper argues that the Pirahã people lack arithmetic not because they lack one-to-one correspondence, but because they lack a symbolic cardinality operator #, which is realized by number-word practices.
motivation: To resolve the apparent paradox that the Pirahã can match objects one-to-one but do not develop counting or arithmetic, by precisely locating the cognitive gap in Frege's theorem.
method: Conceptual analysis of Hume's principle, identifying the cardinality operator # as the crucial component, and supporting the identification with cross-cultural evidence from Nicaraguan homesigners, numerate adults under verbal interference, and cross-linguistic numeral gradients.
result: The Pirahã lack the # operator, which is cognitively realized by stable symbolic token practices (e.g., number words, tally marks), not by the ability to perceive equinumerosity.
conclusion: The cognitive boundary for arithmetic lies in symbolization, not recursion, and the presence of arithmetic across cultures is a gradient depending on the availability of symbolic token practices.

title: Sharp Asymptotic Minimaxity Of The Gavrilov-Benjamini-Sarkar Step-Down Testing Procedure In Sparse Gaussian Sequence Models
authors: Prasenjit Ghosh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the sharp asymptotic minimaxity of the classical Gavrilov-Benjamini-Sarkar (GBS) step-down multiple testing procedure in sparse Gaussian sequence models. Abraham et al. (2024) recently established sharp asymptotic minimax benchmarks for sparse multiple testing under both the classical beta-min framework and more general heterogeneous signal-strength classes. Although several multiple testing procedures attain these benchmarks, corresponding results for the GBS procedure have remained unavailable. We prove that the GBS procedure is sharply asymptotically minimax under both normalized Hamming loss and the combined [MATH] loss over the classical beta-min parameter classes. We further establish a sharp asymptotic upper bound for the normalized Hamming risk over the heterogeneous signal-strength classes and show that the GBS procedure attains the corresponding sharp asymptotic minimax benchmark under the combined [MATH] loss. Our analysis is based on a shifted order-statistic inequality for the GBS critical values together with deterministic and empirical signal-crossing arguments for ordered alternative [MATH]-values. Unlike existing analyses of Benjamini-Hochberg procedures and empirical Bayes [MATH]-value methods, the proposed approach is intrinsic to the geometry of the GBS step-down procedure and avoids localization of a single implicit rejection threshold. Consequently, our results extend sharp asymptotic minimaxity theory to a genuinely step-down multiple testing procedure whose rejection rule depends on the entire ordered sequence of [MATH]-values.
tldr: This paper proves sharp asymptotic minimaxity of the GBS step-down multiple testing procedure in sparse Gaussian sequence models.
motivation: To establish optimality of the GBS procedure in sparse multiple testing, which had not been shown before.
method: Uses a shifted order-statistic inequality and deterministic/empirical signal-crossing arguments for ordered alternative p-values.
result: The GBS procedure is sharply asymptotically minimax under normalized Hamming loss and combined loss over beta-min and heterogeneous signal-strength classes.
conclusion: The GBS procedure achieves sharp asymptotic minimaxity, extending the theory to step-down procedures.

title: Approximation Of Partial Differential Operators On Nikolskii-Besov Functions Classes Of Mixed Smoothness In Domains Of A Certain Kind
authors: S. N. Kudryavtsev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article examines Nikolskii and Besov spaces with norms defined using "[MATH]-averaged" mixed moduli of continuity for functions of appropriate orders, instead of mixed moduli of continuity of known orders for certain mixed derivative functions. The work provides upper and lower estimates for a quantity of the best accuracy of approximation in the S.B.Stechkin problem for partial differential operators on a classes of such functions defined in domains of a certain kind. These estimates are not weaker, but in some cases even stronger than those derived by the author in the problem under consideration for the aforementioned classes of functions on cube [MATH] It also significantly broadens the class of Nikolskii and Besov spaces of mixed smoothness for which mentioned estimates in the problem under consideration have been derived.
tldr: The paper studies approximation of partial differential operators on Nikolskii-Besov function classes of mixed smoothness in domains, which is a topic in classical approximation theory and functional analysis.
motivation: To obtain optimal error estimates for approximating partial differential operators on function spaces with mixed smoothness, extending previous results from the cube to more general domains.
method: The author uses Nikolskii and Besov spaces defined via mixed moduli of continuity and derives upper and lower bounds for the best approximation accuracy in the S.B. Stechkin problem.
result: The estimates are not weaker, and in some cases stronger, than those previously obtained for the cube, and they broaden the class of spaces for which such estimates are known.
conclusion: The work provides improved approximation estimates for partial differential operators on a wider class of function spaces and domains.

title: Higher-Order Derivatives Do Not Accelerate The Computation Of Fixed Points
authors: Ernest K. Ryu Uijeong Jang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Picard iteration converges to the unique fixed point of a [MATH]-contractive operator at a linear rate [MATH], and a lower bound with an affine construction shows that no deterministic method querying only operator values can do better. But what about higher-order methods that query derivatives? A single Jacobian evaluation reveals an affine map entirely, so the affine construction says nothing about higher-order methods. In this work, we show that finite-order derivative information still does not accelerate the worst-case complexity for smooth contractive fixed-point computation. This contrasts with higher-order smooth minimization, where higher-order derivatives do improve worst-case rates for convex and non-convex minimization.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Symplectic Billiards As Minkowski Billiards
authors: Peter Albers, Ana Chavez Caliz, Serge Tabachnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a connection between Minkowski billiards and symplectic billiards, two classes of dynamical systems that have been studied largely independently. We show that the Minkowski billiard map can be described in symplectic terms via reduction from the canonical symplectic structure on [MATH], and that symplectic billiards can be viewed as a ``square root'' of a symplectic version of Minkowski billiards. As an application, we recover several known results on symplectic billiards from the more general Minkowski setting, and extend some of them to higher dimensions and to periodic orbits of even period. In particular, we prove the existence of at least [MATH] [MATH]-periodic symplectic billiard orbits in dimension [MATH].
tldr: This paper establishes a connection between Minkowski billiards and symplectic billiards, showing that the Minkowski billiard map can be described in symplectic terms and that symplectic billiards can be viewed as a square root of a symplectic version of Minkowski billiards.
motivation: To unify two classes of dynamical systems that have been studied independently and to derive results on symplectic billiards from the more general Minkowski setting.
method: The authors use symplectic reduction to describe the Minkowski billiard map and reinterpret symplectic billiards as a square root of a symplectic version of Minkowski billiards.
result: They recover known results on symplectic billiards and extend some to higher dimensions and periodic orbits of even period, proving existence of at least two 2-periodic symplectic billiard orbits in dimension 2.
conclusion: The connection provides a unified framework and yields new results for symplectic billiards.

title: A Semismooth Newton Augmented Lagrangian Method For Sparse Spectral Risk Optimization
authors: Rufeng Xiao, Rujun Jiang, Xudong Li, Defeng Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical risk minimization is a standard and effective paradigm for learning predictive models by minimizing average loss. In high-stakes decision-making, however, an average-loss criterion may underrepresent rare but severe losses. Spectral risk measures (SRMs) provide a principled framework by incorporating weighted order statistics of losses, but the induced nonsmoothness and nonseparability from sorting make the resulting optimization problems challenging. We propose a relative inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method with a semismooth Newton subproblem solver for solving SRM-based optimization problems. Exploiting a dual reformulation and properties of the Moreau envelope, we reduce the subproblems to structured dual-variable formulations, significantly simplifying computation. We provide explicit generalized Jacobian characterizations and tailor the pool adjacent violators algorithm for their efficient evaluation. Numerical results on synthetic and real-data instances show that the proposed method attains lower running times than the tested ADMM baseline while producing comparable stationarity residuals and sparse solutions.
tldr: This paper proposes a semismooth Newton augmented Lagrangian method for sparse spectral risk optimization, a topic in optimization and machine learning.
motivation: Spectral risk measures are important for high-stakes decision-making but lead to challenging nonsmooth optimization problems due to sorting operations.
method: The authors develop a relative inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method with a semismooth Newton subproblem solver, exploiting dual reformulation and Moreau envelope properties.
result: The proposed method achieves lower running times than ADMM on synthetic and real data while producing comparable stationarity residuals and sparse solutions.
conclusion: The method efficiently solves spectral risk optimization problems, offering a practical alternative to existing approaches.

title: A Unified Energy-stable Finite Element Approximation For Evolving Fluidic Biomembranes
authors: Harald Garcke, Robert N\"urnberg, Quan Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a unified finite element method for the dynamics of fluidic biomembranes. The model is governed by the Navier--Stokes equations in the bulk coupled to the surface Navier--Stokes equations on the evolving biomembrane surface, with bending forces arising from the Willmore energy. By allowing the bulk mesh velocity to be independent of the fluid velocity and permitting a free tangential surface velocity, we are able to derive a unified weak formulation of the coupled bulk-surface Navier--Stokes system. To address the bending force, we consider an evolution equation for the curvature and propose a surface arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) weak formulation. Discretization with either fitted or unfitted finite elements leads to well-posed fully discrete linear schemes that are unconditionally energy stable. We present a variety of numerical examples to demonstrate the favourable properties of the proposed methods.
tldr: This paper presents a unified finite element method for simulating the dynamics of fluidic biomembranes, governed by coupled bulk-surface Navier-Stokes equations with bending forces.
motivation: Accurate simulation of fluidic biomembranes is important for understanding biological processes, but existing numerical methods often lack energy stability or require restrictive mesh conditions.
method: The authors derive a unified weak formulation using an arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian approach, allowing independent bulk mesh velocity and free tangential surface velocity, and discretize with fitted or unfitted finite elements to obtain unconditionally energy-stable linear schemes.
result: The proposed methods are shown to be well-posed and unconditionally energy stable, with numerical examples demonstrating favorable properties.
conclusion: The unified finite element approach provides a robust and energy-stable framework for simulating evolving fluidic biomembranes.

title: Metagraph-Based Domain-Decomposed Galerkin Reduced-Order Model
authors: Kyohei Shintate, Naoki Morita, Shigeki Kaneko, Nozomi Magome, Naoto Mitsume
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study proposes a metagraph-based domain-decomposed Galerkin reduced-order model (MBDD-G-ROM) for distributed-memory parallel reduced-order analysis of large-scale problems. The method represents domain-decomposed Galerkin reduced-order models over arbitrary domain decompositions using two graph levels: calculation-point graphs for interactions among discretization points and metagraphs for connectivity among local approximation-space subdomains. In the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based implementation, POD computation subdomains are represented as metanodes, while metaedges encode the block-sparsity induced by overlaps between local POD basis supports. Partitioning the metagraph enables the POD computation subdomains to be decoupled from the parallel computation subdomains, allowing distributed-memory parallelization of both offline and online phases, including reduced-system assembly and iterative linear solution, without requiring the two decompositions to coincide. The metagraph also supports static load balancing through metanode weights that approximate computational costs. The method is evaluated for an unsteady diffusion equation and incompressible Navier-Stokes flow around a three-dimensional cylinder. The results show that MBDD-G-ROM preserves reduced-order solution accuracy while achieving high online parallel efficiency. A load-balancing test further demonstrates that cost-based metanode weights can improve computational efficiency.
tldr: This paper proposes a metagraph-based domain-decomposed Galerkin reduced-order model for parallel reduced-order analysis of large-scale problems.
motivation: Large-scale simulations require efficient reduced-order models that can be parallelized on distributed-memory systems, but existing methods often couple the domain decomposition for POD with that for parallel computation, limiting flexibility and scalability.
method: The method uses two graph levels: calculation-point graphs for discretization point interactions and metagraphs for connectivity among local approximation-space subdomains. Metagraph partitioning decouples POD computation subdomains from parallel computation subdomains, enabling distributed-memory parallelization of both offline and online phases.
result: The method preserves reduced-order solution accuracy while achieving high online parallel efficiency, as demonstrated on an unsteady diffusion equation and incompressible Navier-Stokes flow around a 3D cylinder.
conclusion: The metagraph-based approach provides a flexible and efficient framework for parallel reduced-order modeling, with potential for further optimization through cost-based load balancing.

title: Invariant-domain-preserving Limiting With Adaptive Mesh Refinement For Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Element Methods
authors: Benjamin Bolm, Andr\'es M. Rueda-Ram\'irez, Dmitri Kuzmin, Gregor J. Gassner
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an invariant-domain-preserving (IDP) treatment of nonconforming interfaces for Legendre--Gauss--Lobatto Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Element Methods (LGL-DGSEM) with adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) on Cartesian meshes. The proposed methodology extends recently developed convex limiting and graph-viscosity frameworks for DGSEM to meshes containing hanging nodes. Starting from a conservative mortar formulation, we derive low-order interface fluxes that satisfy the requirements of invariant-domain-preserving discretizations. To avoid the excessive diffusion associated with fully connected mortar couplings, a sparsification strategy based on LGL subcell characteristic functions is introduced, yielding compact interface stencils. The resulting mortar fluxes remain conservative, reduce to the standard conforming formulation on matching interfaces, and naturally fit into graph-viscosity-based low-order schemes used for convex limiting. The proposed construction provides the missing ingredient required to combine high-order DGSEM discretizations, invariant-domain-preserving limiting, and adaptive mesh refinement within a unified framework for nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws. We provide numerical verifications of the properties of the proposed scheme and run challenging simulations that require positivity limiting and shock-capturing.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for preserving invariant domains in high-order discontinuous Galerkin simulations with adaptive mesh refinement.
motivation: High-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws can produce unphysical oscillations; invariant-domain-preserving (IDP) schemes ensure physical bounds but have not been extended to nonconforming interfaces with hanging nodes.
method: The authors extend convex limiting and graph-viscosity frameworks to nonconforming interfaces using a conservative mortar formulation and a sparsification strategy based on LGL subcell characteristic functions.
result: The proposed mortar fluxes are conservative, reduce to standard conforming fluxes on matching interfaces, and integrate naturally with graph-viscosity-based low-order schemes for convex limiting.
conclusion: The work provides the missing ingredient for combining high-order DGSEM, IDP limiting, and AMR for nonlinear hyperbolic conservation laws, verified through numerical simulations.

title: Analytic Integration Of Metric-valued Functions In Lipschitz Free Spaces
authors: Roger Arnau, \'alvaro Gonz\'alez Cort\'es, Enrique A. S\'anchez P\'erez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an integration theory for functions taking values in a metric space. Following a Bochner-type construction, we define the concept of free integral as an element of the Lipschitz-free space [MATH]. We establish the main properties of this integral, including duality formulas, and the study of the resulting space of free integrable functions. We also cover when the metric space is a Banach space: in this setting, the free integral has an interpretable decomposition generalising the Bochner integral. We then connect the free integral with the geometry of [MATH] by showing that it always produces convex integrals of molecules. This allows to study extremal properties within the unit ball of [MATH]. Finally, we provide a detailed example to illustrate the framework we develop.
tldr: This paper develops an integration theory for metric-valued functions using Lipschitz free spaces, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend Bochner integration to functions taking values in a metric space, providing a framework for integration in Lipschitz free spaces.
method: They define a free integral as an element of the Lipschitz free space, establish duality formulas, and study the space of free integrable functions, including the special case when the metric space is a Banach space.
result: The free integral always produces convex integrals of molecules, enabling the study of extremal properties within the unit ball of the Lipschitz free space.
conclusion: The paper contributes to functional analysis and metric geometry, but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Efficient Pareto-Front Generation For Electric Machines Using Iga And Second Order Derivatives
authors: Theodor Komann, Michael Wiesheu, Stefan Ulbrich, Sebastian Sch\"ops, Peter Gangl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multiobjective optimization of electric machines always involves a trade-off caused by various competing objectives such as performance and cost. A suitable design is usually determined by comparing variants from the Pareto front, which has been generated by a large number of simulation runs. This paper addresses the efficient generation of the Pareto front using a continuation method based on a homotopy method that exploits second-order derivative information to achieve superlinear convergence, enabling the fast generation of new Pareto-optimal points within only a few iterations. A key contribution is the derivation of formulas to compute the Hessian with respect to geometry parameters and shape, thus enabling direct modifications of the motor geometry in the context of Isogeometric Analysis. We apply our method to nonlinear 2D magnetostatic simulations of a permanent magnet synchronous motor and demonstrate its effectiveness by optimizing the cost, mean torque and torque ripple of the motor. Compared to a first-order optimization method, this approach reduces the number of iterations and function evaluations needed, making the pareto optimization fast and efficient.
tldr: This paper presents a method for efficient Pareto front generation in electric machine design using isogeometric analysis and second-order derivatives.
motivation: Multiobjective optimization of electric machines involves trade-offs between competing objectives like performance and cost, requiring many simulation runs to generate the Pareto front.
method: A continuation method based on homotopy that exploits second-order derivative information (Hessian) to achieve superlinear convergence, with formulas for Hessian computation in isogeometric analysis.
result: Applied to a permanent magnet synchronous motor, the method reduces iterations and function evaluations compared to first-order optimization.
conclusion: The approach enables fast and efficient generation of Pareto-optimal points for electric machine design.

title: A Study Of Holes: Topological Analysis Reveals Crowd Dynamics Regimes In A Bidirectional Corridor Scenario
authors: Gerta K\"oster Sabrina Desiree Kern
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study harnesses topological analysis in an attempt to reveal structure in the dynamics of a crowd. Topology and in particular persistent homology characterizes relational structures in data through the number of connected components and holes, that is, a loop of pairwise connection with no connections across it. We apply this universal data analysis method to a simulated time series of individual pedestrian positions of a crowd moving through a wide corridor -- either uni- or bidirectional. We consider two pedestrians to be connected, when they are sufficiently close. This approach leads to two matrices containing the persistence signatures for the whole time series, so-called CROCKERs. Despite the high level of data abstraction, the CROCKERs' first two principal components on time-delayed positional data show a clear separation of the different parameter configurations. This holds up to symmetry. Our results support our claim that persistent homology is a useful tool to characterize crowd dynamics without introducing any prior assumptions about the detectable spatio-temporal patterns.
tldr: This paper uses topological data analysis (persistent homology) to characterize crowd dynamics in a bidirectional corridor scenario.
motivation: The authors aim to reveal structure in crowd dynamics without prior assumptions, using topological methods to identify regimes.
method: They apply persistent homology to simulated pedestrian trajectories, constructing CROCKER matrices and performing PCA on time-delayed positional data.
result: The first two principal components of the CROCKERs clearly separate different parameter configurations, demonstrating the utility of persistent homology for crowd dynamics.
conclusion: Persistent homology is a useful tool for characterizing crowd dynamics without introducing prior assumptions about spatio-temporal patterns.

title: Closed-form Fractional Radial Links For Elliptical Mahalanobis Discriminant Analysis
authors: Serhii Zabolotnii
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study binary classification under shared-generator elliptical class-conditional distributions. The log-likelihood ratio is an additive function of the two squared Mahalanobis radii, with radial link [MATH]; QDA is recovered only when this link is affine. We derive the Bayes radial-link family from the within-class radius law and estimate it by a finite fractional-power stochastic-polynomial projection instead of tuning a generic spline. The link is identifiable from the radius law, the plug-in estimator is [MATH]-consistent and asymptotically normal under finite-moment regularity conditions, and the induced classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal in an iterated sieve limit. The structural bridge, GAM membership, and identity-link/affine-generator dichotomy are verified in Lean 4 without unproven placeholders. Against the global Mahalanobis-GAM of Ghosh et al. (2025), reimplemented with mgcv REML splines at equal input budget, the derived link is never significantly worse on three UCI benchmarks and is decisively better on breast_cancer ([MATH] global, [MATH] global+local). Across six real financial series under temporal-dependence-robust validation, it is never significantly worse than the fitted GAM and is significantly better on three of five heavy-tailed series plus the light-tailed control. Relative to QDA, it improves the heaviest-tailed series (oil [MATH], S&P 500 [MATH], JPY/USD [MATH]) and ties elsewhere. A closed-form rate simulation corroborates the [MATH] rate and the predicted excess-risk dichotomy between QDA's approximation-limited floor and the derived link's vanishing excess risk. The contribution is no significant loss relative to a tuned global GAM without spline smoothing-parameter selection, plus improved accuracy over QDA where generator curvature matters.
tldr: This paper develops a closed-form fractional radial link for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis, improving binary classification under elliptical class-conditional distributions.
motivation: The authors aim to derive a Bayes-optimal radial link function for classification under elliptical distributions, overcoming limitations of QDA and generic spline-based methods.
method: They derive the Bayes radial-link family from the within-class radius law and estimate it via a finite fractional-power stochastic-polynomial projection, establishing consistency and asymptotic normality.
result: The proposed classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal and outperforms QDA on heavy-tailed financial series while being competitive with a tuned global GAM on UCI benchmarks.
conclusion: The closed-form link offers improved accuracy over QDA when generator curvature matters, with no significant loss relative to a tuned GAM, and is validated on real data.

title: Transcendental Correspondences: When Fuchsian Groups Take Over Basins Of Entire Maps
authors: Kostiantyn Drach, Sabyasachi Mukherjee, Leticia Pardo-Sim\'on
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we initiate a systematic study of [MATH] holomorphic correspondences that naturally arise as conformal combinations (matings) of transcendental entire maps with Fuchsian groups. This construction parallels the recent theory of finite-degree algebraic correspondences associated with rational maps. Our correspondence combines the dynamics of a transcendental entire function outside a distinguished attracting/parabolic basin with the action of a compatible Fuchsian group within it. We show that the resulting correspondence is the composition of a M\"obius involution and the deleted covering correspondence of a meromorphic function having exactly one simple pole. When the transcendental entire function has finitely many singular values, so does this meromorphic function, and its line complex can be described explicitly.
tldr: This paper studies transcendental correspondences arising from matings of entire maps with Fuchsian groups, a topic in complex dynamics.
motivation: To initiate a systematic study of holomorphic correspondences that combine transcendental entire dynamics with Fuchsian group actions.
method: The authors construct conformal combinations (matings) of transcendental entire maps with Fuchsian groups, analyzing the resulting correspondence as a composition of a Möbius involution and a deleted covering correspondence of a meromorphic function.
result: The correspondence is shown to be the composition of a Möbius involution and the deleted covering correspondence of a meromorphic function with exactly one simple pole; when the entire function has finitely many singular values, the meromorphic function also has finitely many singular values and its line complex is described explicitly.
conclusion: This work extends the theory of algebraic correspondences to transcendental settings, providing a framework for studying dynamics of entire maps and Fuchsian groups.

title: Optimal Control Problems Of Stochastic Volterra Integral Equations Under Volatility Ambiguity
authors: Mingshang Hu Bingru Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal control problems for stochastic Volterra integral equations driven by G-Brownian motion under Volatility Ambiguity. With the help of G-stochastic analysis techniques and the weak convergence methods, we obtain the variation of the cost functional and the variational inequality. Under the convexity assumptions, we establish the stochastic maximum principle, which serves as both a necessary and sufficient condition for optimal control.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control problems for stochastic Volterra integral equations driven by G-Brownian motion under volatility ambiguity, establishing a stochastic maximum principle.
motivation: The paper aims to extend optimal control theory to stochastic Volterra integral equations with volatility ambiguity, which is a mathematical finance problem.
method: The authors use G-stochastic analysis techniques and weak convergence methods to derive the variation of the cost functional and variational inequality, then establish the stochastic maximum principle under convexity assumptions.
result: A stochastic maximum principle is obtained that serves as both necessary and sufficient conditions for optimal control.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for optimal control of stochastic Volterra equations under model uncertainty, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Delay Violation Probability Modeling For 5g Systems With Harq Operation
authors: Sangwon Seo, Vishnu N Moothedath, Niloofar Mehrnia, Neda Petreska, Bernhard Kloiber, James Gross
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Meeting the growing demand for quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees in 5G networks requires an accurate characterization of delay performance, commonly captured by the delay violation probability (DVP) at a specified delay target. Although hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) is a fundamental reliability mechanism in wireless systems and is central to supporting QoS, many existing approaches to DVP prediction for HARQ remain overly simplified. In particular, they omit important delay components and adopt assumptions that do not reflect the operation of HARQ in slot-based systems such as 5G. Consequently, these models can substantially underestimate the DVP, especially under stringent latency requirements, where the contribution of the neglected components becomes critical. To address this gap, we develop a tractable DVP characterization for 5G HARQ that accounts for queueing, transmission, decoding, and feedback delay, as well as the contribution of Control Signaling (CS) transmissions to the overall delay, under practical timing assumptions consistent with 3GPP operation. Moreover, we incorporate parallel packet transmissions that proceed without waiting for earlier packets to succeed, an essential HARQ behavior frequently overlooked in prior work. Using tools from queueing theory and Markov analysis, we then derive upper bounds on the DVP and validate them against ns-3 5G-LENA simulations.
tldr: This paper models delay violation probability for 5G systems with HARQ operation using queueing theory and Markov analysis.
motivation: Existing DVP models for HARQ omit important delay components and underestimate DVP under stringent latency requirements.
method: The authors develop a tractable DVP characterization accounting for queueing, transmission, decoding, feedback, and control signaling delays, and incorporate parallel packet transmissions. They derive upper bounds using queueing theory and Markov analysis, validated via ns-3 5G-LENA simulations.
result: The proposed model provides more accurate DVP bounds compared to simplified models, especially under strict latency targets.
conclusion: Accurate DVP modeling is crucial for QoS guarantees in 5G, and the proposed approach better captures HARQ operation realities.

title: Discrete Imprecise Copulas And Alternating Sign Matrices
authors: Toma\v{z} Ko\v{s}ir, Elisa Perrone, Nik Stopar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study discrete quasi-copulas and discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range, which naturally correspond to alternating sign matrices. We show that this family is invariant under all defect transformations on quasi-copulas and give a constructive proof demonstrating that discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range do not, in general, avoid sure loss. In contrast, we show that discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range that correspond to dense alternating sign matrices are always coherent, and hence avoid sure loss.
tldr: This paper studies discrete imprecise copulas and their connection to alternating sign matrices, focusing on mathematical properties like invariance under defect transformations and coherence conditions.
motivation: To understand the structure of discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range and their relationship to alternating sign matrices, and to determine when such copulas avoid sure loss.
method: The authors define discrete quasi-copulas and imprecise copulas, show their correspondence to alternating sign matrices, and analyze properties such as invariance under defect transformations and coherence using dense alternating sign matrices.
result: Discrete imprecise copulas of minimal range are invariant under all defect transformations, but they do not generally avoid sure loss; however, those corresponding to dense alternating sign matrices are always coherent.
conclusion: The work provides a characterization of a specific family of imprecise copulas, linking them to combinatorial objects, but the topic is far from the user's research interests in quantum information theory.

title: Proof Of Execution: Runtime Verification For Governed Ai Agent Actions
authors: George Kang James Rhodes
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent systems increasingly execute rather than advise. When an AI agent queries regulated data, invokes effectful tools, and mutates persistent state, correctness is not captured by whether a terminal output looks plausible. The operative questions are whether each step was authorized under a contract, whether the recorded history is tamper-evident, and whether the trajectory can be reconstructed deterministically. We formalize this as runtime proof of execution. An execution is a triple [MATH]: a contract [MATH], an Execution Causal Event Stream (ECES) [MATH], and a replay context [MATH]. A well-formedness predicate and five validator-checkable invariants form the PoE validity predicate. Five semantic guarantees describe authorization, path compliance, null effect on deny, history integrity, and replayability. We prove soundness under explicit cryptographic and deployment assumptions: any PPT adversary that produces a PoE-valid execution violating a semantic guarantee yields a signature forgery, a hash collision, or a quantified deployment-failure event. The Prime Execution Model (PEM) separates planning, enforcement, effect, and recordkeeping into distinct authority planes; a lemma reduces trace completeness to Effector-exclusive credentialing. An Execution Attestation Certificate is issued only when PoE = 1. In a single-node TypeScript prototype, PoE adds approximately 2.7 ms on a minimal flow and 4.4% overhead on concurrent batch workloads; a standard eight-event trace compresses to approximately 1.1 KB; injected Gateway-bypass and trace-mutation attacks are rejected. PoE does not replace consensus, TEEs, or zkVMs; it binds authorization, effect, history, and replay into a single runtime-checkable object so that governed execution becomes attestable under contract.
tldr: This paper introduces a runtime verification framework for AI agent actions, focusing on authorization, tamper-evident history, and deterministic replay.
motivation: As AI agents execute actions beyond mere advice, ensuring each step is authorized and recorded becomes critical for governance and accountability.
method: The authors formalize a Proof of Execution (PoE) as a triple (contract, event stream, replay context) with five validator-checkable invariants, and implement a Prime Execution Model separating planning, enforcement, effect, and recordkeeping.
result: A TypeScript prototype shows PoE adds ~2.7 ms overhead per minimal flow and 4.4% on concurrent batches; an eight-event trace compresses to ~1.1 KB; attacks are rejected.
conclusion: PoE provides a runtime-checkable object that binds authorization, effect, history, and replay, making governed execution attestable under contract without replacing consensus or TEEs.

title: Optimism As A Vulnerability: Deceptive Stackelberg Control Of Ucb Bandit Followers
authors: \c{s}uayp Talha Kocabay, Kerem Yal\c{c}{\i}n, Talha R\"uzgar Akku\c{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2607.05423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) algorithms guarantee sublinear regret for agents learning unknown stochastic environments, yet the same principle that makes them statistically efficient (optimism in the face of uncertainty) induces a predictable strategic vulnerability against an omniscient adaptive leader. Classical strong Stackelberg equilibrium (SSE) assumes that the follower immediately best-responds to the leader's committed mixed action; it therefore supplies no mechanism-design prescription for a leader facing a boundedly rational follower who constructs and acts on empirical reward histories. We formalize this conflict in a finite-horizon repeated Stackelberg game and give exact constructive proofs for a deceptive leader mechanism. In a honeypot phase, the leader pays a finite signaling cost to inflate the UCB index of a designated follower action. In a trap phase, the leader switches to a selfish action distribution while the follower remains locked into the designated action because the manipulated empirical history and exploration bonus dominate competing indices. Under explicit separation and payoff assumptions, the leader's cumulative utility strictly exceeds the classical SSE ceiling, and the manipulation cost is bounded by a regret calculation of order [MATH]. The results identify a formal incompatibility between static equilibrium prescriptions and dynamically learned empirical incentives.
